hints: Focus on what each number tells you, the bottom number is protons, the top minus bottom is neutrons, and charge changes electrons.
Work out the three numbers for the neutral aluminium atom first, it is a quick check of protons = electrons.
For each ion, remember to add electrons for a negative charge and subtract for a positive charge, then look for the one where all three counts match nothing else.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three rules**

Great start, let's get the tools ready. These three rules work every time.

$$\text{protons} = \text{atomic number (bottom number)}$$ $$\text{neutrons} = \text{mass number - atomic number}$$ $$\text{electrons} = \text{protons - charge}$$

**Check the neutral atom**

For $^{27}_{13}\text{Al}$, there is no charge so it is neutral. Protons = 13, neutrons = $27 - 13 = 14$, electrons = 13.

Protons and electrons are the same here, so not all different.

**Check the negative ions**

For $^{35}_{17}\text{Cl}^{-}$: protons = 17, neutrons = $35 - 17 = 18$, electrons = $17 - (-1) = 18$. Neutrons and electrons are both 18.

For $^{32}_{16}\text{S}^{2-}$: protons = 16, neutrons = $32 - 16 = 16$, electrons = $16 - (-2) = 18$. Protons and neutrons are both 16.

**Check the positive ion and conclude**

For $^{39}_{19}\text{K}^{+}$: protons = 19, neutrons = $39 - 19 = 20$, electrons = $19 - (+1) = 18$.

Here we have 19 protons, 20 neutrons and 18 electrons. All three are different, so this is the answer.

options.A: Incorrect. $^{27}_{13}\text{Al}$ is neutral, so protons = electrons = 13, while neutrons = 14. Only two values are different, not all three.
options.B: Incorrect. $^{35}_{17}\text{Cl}^{-}$ has 17 protons, 18 neutrons and 18 electrons (one extra electron for the 1- charge). Neutrons and electrons are the same.
options.C: Incorrect. $^{32}_{16}\text{S}^{2-}$ has 16 protons, 16 neutrons and 18 electrons (two extra electrons for the 2- charge). Protons and neutrons are the same.
options.D: Correct. $^{39}_{19}\text{K}^{+}$ has 19 protons, 20 neutrons (39 - 19) and 18 electrons (19 - 1 for the 1+ charge). 19, 20 and 18 are all different.
